items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to reporting on handgun licenses
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:A10894

TITLE  OF  BILL:    An  act  to  amend the executive law, in relation to
reporting on handgun licenses

PURPOSE: To require the Division of Criminal Justice Services to  report
on the administration of certain laws related to handgun licenses.

SUMMARY  OF PROVISIONS:   Section 1 of the bill amends the executive law
by adding a new section 837-s to require an annual report by  the  Divi-
sion  of  Criminal  Justice Services on the administration, function and
effectiveness of administration of  the  laws  regarding  the  issuance,
modification  of,  amendment  to,  and revocation of handgun licenses in
each city with a population greater than one million  and  each  county.
The  report  shall include a description of how applications for handgun
licenses are received, processed, reviewed, and  approved  or  rejected;
information on personnel and staffing employed to process and administer
handgun  licenses;  for  each  of the preceding five calendar years, the
number of handgun  licenses  issued,  the  number  of  handgun  licenses
revoked,  the number of handgun licenses amended, the number of applica-
tions for handgun licenses rejected, and the number of handgun  licenses
outstanding  at  the  end  of  the  year;  and a detailed description of
instruction, if any, offered to handgun license applicants or licensees.

Section 2 of the bill sets forth the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION: The State Police currently maintains a master database of
all records of handgun transactions and pistol license issuances, amend-
ments, cancellations, and revocations throughout the State, a repository
for the mandated "records of transaction" that accompany  sales  by  gun
dealers  or  between private residents. This information helps the State
Police quickly establish the current  ownership  of  a  weapon  and  the
legality  of a person's possession of a weapon. This bill would build on
the efforts already in place to accumulate this data  by  requiring  the
Division  of Criminal Justice Services to submit an annual report to the
legislature and the governor that presents statistical information based
on this data on a county by county basis. The bill would also provide  a
useful  description  of  the  handgun  licensing policies and procedures
followed by each  issuing  authority  throughout  the  State.  Both  the
statistics  and  the  overview of policies and procedures would increase
transparency and provide a helpful backdrop for policy discussions among
legislators and the public at large.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPACT ON THE STATE: Minimal

EFFECTIVE DATE: This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Requires the division of criminal justice services to report on handgun licenses.
